messages:
Noah: quick follow-up from today's all-hands infra segment. wanted to capture a couple of less-covered items: capacity smoothing, maintenance drains, and how reclamation from burst works. posting here so we have a single place for action items.

Elena: thanks  first Q: what exactly do we mean by 'capacity smoothing'? teams heard that term but not the details.

Noah: good call  capacity smoothing is the autoscaler's short-term hedging mechanism. instead of instant scale-ups on a spike, it applies a smoothing window (default 90s) and a small headroom buffer to avoid flip-flopping. goal is fewer churn-induced cold starts.

Kai: follow-up: does smoothing change how we account for buffer targets per region? some oncall folks want concrete numbers.

Noah: smoothing doesn't change target buffers. we maintain region buffer % (default 12% business hours, 6% off-hours) but smoothing shapes the scale decisions to reach those targets gracefully. we'll add a small doc section with math and examples.

Maya: maintenance drains: ops note  when a zone is scheduled for maintenance we mark it as 'draining' and the router prefers fallbacks. we also reserve a maintenance window buffer so we don't push customers to failovers immediately.

Elena: curious about GPU reclamation from burst pools  when we need to remove preemptible GPUs from burst, how do we pick which workloads to evict?

Noah: eviction priority: 1) non-reserved, non-enterprise routes, 2) best-effort quantized variants, 3) requests with `cost_protection:true` are deprioritized last. we send a pre-eviction header to clients (`x-rw-evict-warning`) with 10s TTL to let SDKs gracefully reconnect.

Sales_Rahul: for customers, what are the billing / SLA implications if we evict and they get routed to a different region? will they see credits?

Maya: billing: customers are billed by the serving region. SLA credits: if a customer with reserved capacity experiences failover due to a maintenance drain within their own region, we consider a partial SLA credit if the failure violates reserved latency SLOs. exact calc is in the SLA playbook; we'll surface a short FAQ for sales.

Kai: can orgs reserve a 'soft hold' on burst capacity for short promos to avoid eviction?

Noah: yes  introducing a new knob `reservation_window` that can be set for short-term holds (1h, 4h) at an org-level. it costs a small premium and uses the burst pool reservation logic. we'll open a billing PR to describe pricing options.

Elena: maintenance automation Q: can we schedule rolling drains such that we never drop below a region redundancy threshold?

Maya: ops currently supports staged drains with configurable redundancy thresholds per region. default is maintain at least 2 active racks with GPUs before draining a third. we'll expose the threshold in the infra calendar for visibility.

Noah: SDK behaviour: when eviction or drain happens, SDKs should retry with exponential backoff and respect `x-rw-evict-warning`. we'll add a small helper in the JS and Python clients to surface a reconnect modal for streaming apps.

Sales_Rahul: last customer question: can we offer a 'no-cross-region' guarantee as an add-on so enterprise customers never pay cross-region rates?

Maya: yes  product offers `pin_by_org: true` and `fallback_policy: none` for strict residency. we can also offer `cost_protection` to prefer cheaper fallbacks but that doesn't enforce residency. greenfield enterprise bundles can include guaranteed regional isolation with pricing adjustments.

infra-bot: [deploy] staged-drain scheduler v1 rolled out by @Noah  changelist: 10421  link: https://redwood.internal/infra/changes/10421 :white_check_mark:

Kai: action items?

Noah: 1) publish a one-pager explaining capacity smoothing + worked examples (owner: Noah) by EOD tomorrow, 2) add `x-rw-evict-warning` header spec to SDK docs (owner: Kai) by mid-week, 3) draft billing blurb and SLA FAQ for sales (owner: Maya) by Friday, 4) expose region drain threshold in infra calendar (owner: Ops) next sprint. tagging @Maya @Kai.

Maya: ack  I'll draft the SLA FAQ and coordinate with billing.

Kai: ack  will add the SDK helper and a small example.

Elena: thanks  this clears up a lot. please emoji-react if you see anything missing. :thumbsup:
